t: In front of you is the Edith Cavell Memorial, by the sculptor Sir George Frampton, just outside the northeast corner of Trafalgar Square. Edith Cavell was a British nurse who treated wounded soldiers from both sides without discrimination in the First World War, and helped some two hundred Allied soldiers escape from German-occupied Belgium. She was arrested, court-martialled and shot, and the execution drew worldwide condemnation. Frampton, a leading figure in the New Sculpture movement, also made the Peter Pan statue in Kensington Gardens. The memorial stands next to the first headquarters of the British Red Cross.
